evidence: Tac. Ann. 1.61: aggerēs ūmidō palūdum … impōnere (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: “A crossing on foot”; Lewis & Short has agger for a causeway through a swamp.

terms.gloss: the raised bed of a road, a causeway
evidence: Verg. A. 5.273: viae dēprēnsus in aggere serpēns (Lewis & Short s.v. agger)
terms.comment: Agger is earth heaped up, a mound or rampart; with viae (Vergil and Tacitus) the built-up road itself.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Lewis & Short: agger
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
